fields.title: Estimate Orders of Magnitude
fields.keyTakeaway: A back-of-the-envelope estimate gives an order of magnitude in five minutes and usually answers a product question rather than a technical one.
fields.sections/0/blocks/0/text: Do we need to store the view history of all users for a year? How much is that?
fields.sections/1/blocks/0/text: A PM who cannot estimate an order of magnitude asks the team questions whose answers take a day—and gets them a day later. One who can filters out the unrealistic immediately and comes with questions that actually require analysis.
fields.sections/2/blocks/0/text: [[back-of-the-envelope|Back-of-the-envelope estimation]] gives an [[order-of-magnitude|order of magnitude]]—a power of ten. Kilobytes, megabytes, or terabytes; seconds, minutes, or hours. Precision within factors is not needed, precision in orders of magnitude is critical.
fields.sections/2/blocks/2/rows/0/0: Database row with a dozen fields
fields.sections/2/blocks/2/rows/4/0: Network request inside a data center
fields.sections/2/blocks/3/text: Method: break into multiplications, round to one significant digit, calculate, check for plausibility.
fields.sections/2/blocks/4/text: Example from the question: 180k active × 40 views per day × 365 days × 400 bytes ≈ 1.05 TB per year. The order is terabytes, not gigabytes or petabytes. Then the decision: a terabyte can be stored, but it is noticeable, and we should think about retention periods.
fields.sections/2/blocks/5/text: Check rule: **if the result differs from expectations by more than 10x, it is likely a calculation error rather than a discovery.**
fields.sections/3/blocks/0/text: Three estimates that changed product decisions.
fields.sections/3/blocks/1/text: *"Store cart snapshot on every change."* 180k × 8 changes × 30 days × 600 bytes ≈ 26 GB per month, 300 GB per year. Too much for a feature used by a handful of people. Dropped.
fields.sections/3/blocks/2/text: *"Show product price history for a year."* 60k products × 2 changes per day × 365 × 100 bytes ≈ 4.4 GB. Acceptable. Built it.
fields.sections/3/blocks/3/text: *"Send a push to everyone when a favorited product drops in price."* 1.2M subscriptions, with typical price drops affecting 3%—36 thousand pushes at once. At two drops per day—72 thousand. Not about storage, but about spam. Changed the product rule: no more than one push per day per person, with aggregation.
fields.sections/3/blocks/4/text: The third case is telling: the estimate was about tech, but the conclusion turned out to be product-related.
fields.sections/4/blocks/0/text: An estimate does not replace measurement where precision matters: cost calculation for a budget requires real data. It answers the question "is it even worth discussing".
fields.sections/5/blocks/0/text: A back-of-the-envelope estimate gives an order of magnitude in five minutes and usually answers a product question rather than a technical one.
